children: By Anand Gopal R
Canada's main stock index rose on Wednesday as strong results from US cloud firm CoreWeave revived enthusiasm for the AI trade, while a rebound in oil prices helped lift energy stocks.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index
was up 0.53% at 36,363.05 points by 10:44 a.m. ET (1544 GMT).
Canadian technology stocks
climbed 1.8%, with Celestica
and BlackBerry
advancing 7.5% and 4.3%, respectively
CoreWeave
, which was at the center of a recent AI selloff, posted strong quarterly results late on Tuesday, helping ease concerns about heavy AI spending at a time when borrowing costs are rising
The Nvidia-backed
company, whose shares were up 21.4%, said it expects to become profitable in the first half of 2028

"We had a big shock last week, and we're coming through it. This week, we also have the major news of the Anthropic IPO. I think there will be a concerted effort to keep markets higher so that the IPO goes off without a hitch,” said Greg Taylor, chief investment officer at PenderFund Capital Management
The energy sector
advanced 2.2%, tracking a 3.4% jump in Brent crude
after Iran's security chief said Tehran would not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country
Among stocks, specialty label and packaging firm CCL Industries
rose 2.6% after beating quarterly sales estimates
Boyd Group
tumbled 11.1% after the collision repair operator missed third-quarter adjusted profit estimates
Lithium Americas
fell 7.8% after increasing the cost estimate for the first phase of its Thacker Pass lithium project in Nevada by 31% to $3.83 billion, citing higher labor, construction and logistics costs
